longForm.overview:
🔈 is the emoji of audio coded speaker read — a clean speaker-pulse shape, the audio filled-in silhouette, and the universal 'audio speaker' tag for volume-marker. Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded speaker read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded speaker read, 🔈 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate audio coded speaker — a 'audio 🔈' volume-marker marker or a 'speaker-pulse pulse 🔈' volume-marker reveal. The audio fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern volume-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as audio coded rather than literal speaker-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🔈 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate volume-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'audio 🔈' volume-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'speaker-pulse pulse 🔈' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'audio coded 🔈' list thread. The audio fill cue is what makes the emoji feel audio coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'audio coded speaker moment.'

What separates 🔈 from the rest of the shape family is the audio register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'audio coded speaker,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 🔈 travels especially well on partner volume-marker markers, volume-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with audio energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:

Avoid 🔈 in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the audio energy feels off. A 'audio 🔈' message works for volume-marker marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 🔈 when you want to communicate a different color. The audio coded register is too audio-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
